_note: v2 hook overrides for le camping (B30_camping). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text, so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_lanterne_noun.hook: Like English 'lantern', said lahn-TEHRN: a glowing LANTERN hangs from a branch at the edge of the woods, and the moths line up to dance around it.
fr_lanterne_noun.why: The painting shows a glowing camp lantern hanging from a branch with dancing moths, not a camper turning on a paper lantern.

fr_allumette_noun.hook: A MATCH flares as a boy kneeling on a little blue loo mat ("a-loo-MET") in the grass lights a candle.
fr_allumette_noun.why: The painting is outdoors at the campsite (boy on a little blue mat lighting a candle), not in a dark bathroom; the loo-mat sound hook is kept.

fr_mendiant_noun.hook: A BEGGAR in a patched coat sits in the back of a van, mending his coat and yawning ("mahn-DYAHN"); a child brings him a loaf of bread.
fr_mendiant_noun.why: Painted at the back of a van at the campsite instead of by a bakery.

fr_cabane_noun.hook: Like English 'cabin', said kah-BAHN: two children sit in their own little HUT up an oak tree, their very own cabane, with a rope ladder to climb in.
fr_cabane_noun.why: The painting shows the children already inside the finished tree hut, not nailing planks.

fr_cantine_noun.hook: Like English 'canteen', said kahn-TEEN: a hungry TEEN at the campsite CANTEEN stacks a wobbly tower of bean CANS on the counter.
fr_cantine_noun.why: The painted tower of cans stands on the canteen counter rather than on a tray.

fr_randonnee_noun.hook: A family with rucksacks sets off on a HIKE, humming a RONDO ("ron-do"), while their pony neighs "NAY!"
fr_randonnee_noun.why: No music notes are painted over the hikers, so the singing becomes humming; the pony is there.

fr_pli_noun.hook: A FOLD in a map: two scouts kneel over a big map with deep creases, and one begs, with a plea ("PLEE"), to fold it right.
fr_pli_noun.why: The painting shows two scouts with the creased map (the source hook has one scout).

fr_camping_noun.hook: Like English 'camping', said kahn-PING: a boy goes CAMPING, and every time he hammers a tent peg in it PINGS like a little bell.
fr_camping_noun.why: One boy hammers the ringing pegs in the painting, not a whole family.

fr_fumeur_noun.hook: Text plaque only: nothing is painted but the small blank brass-framed plaque on a wooden post by the tents; it stands for the word SMOKER (FUMEUR, "few-MUHR", like 'a FEW MORE').
ex: Il n'y a aucun fumeur dans notre camping.
There isn't a single smoker at our campsite.
fr_fumeur_noun.why: Museum plaque word (no smoking rule): the old no-smoking sign was repainted as a blank brass-framed plaque, so nothing is depicted and the hook describes the plaque.

fr_kit_noun.hook: Like English 'kit', said KEET: a camping KIT lies open on a mossy shelf of the old stump, full of tiny tools, and a curious hedgehog peeks in.
fr_kit_noun.why: The painting shows the opened kit with a hedgehog beside it; the tiny tent stands on top of the stump rather than coming out of the kit.

fr_retrait_noun.hook: Like English 'retreat', said ruh-TREH: two little campers beat a hasty RETREAT from a skunk, spilling a TRAY of marshmallows as they run.
fr_retrait_noun.why: Same scene as the source; wording matches the two painted campers.

fr_boucle_noun.hook: Sounds like 'buckle', said BOOKL: a girl's big LOOP of curly hair is fastened with a shiny gold BUCKLE, and gold hoop EARRINGS (des boucles d'oreilles) dangle below.
fr_boucle_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25: the 'curl that loops like a buckle' hook was unclear; the painting now shows a real gold buckle holding her hair loop.

fr_feu_noun.hook: Sounds like 'fur', said FEUH: a bear warms his FUR at a SMALL cosy campfire while toasting a marshmallow. Le feu is a little fire you light on purpose; a whole building ablaze is un incendie.
fr_feu_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25: feu and incendie needed a visible distinction; the bear's campfire was made small.

fr_incendie_noun.hook: Like English 'incendiary', said an-sahn-DEE: a whole BARN is ablaze on the far hill, huge flames roaring from its roof and windows, while firefighters hose it down and the cows watch safely. Un incendie is a BIG blaze that eats a building; the bear's little campfire is only un feu.
fr_incendie_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25: feu and incendie needed a visible distinction; the barn is now a big building blaze.
